title: Communication style as WAI protocol layer
resolution_reason: Communication consistency is essential for multi-agent collaboration

alternatives_considered.option: Leave communication style to individual agent discretion
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Results in inconsistent responses, confusion across sessions, poor UX

alternatives_considered.option: Add Communication Style section to hub/BRIEF.md + preference Lug type
alternatives_considered.reasoning: Consistent with WAI patterns, inheritable via cascade, evolves via observations

summary: WAI is a communications protocol with three layers: human↔agent↔agent. Added Communication Style section to hub/BRIEF.md defining response format, tone matching, and agent-to-agent communication patterns. Extended Lug schema with 'preference' type to capture communication and workflow preferences. Preferences feed apprenticeship loop and periodically consolidate into BRIEF updates.

title: Verification responses should be concise and numbered
observation: Three spokes (framework, website, ezorg-email) responded to identical verification prompt with wildly different formats (verbose prose, detailed reports, sectioned structures)
context: User ran WAI v2 verification prompt across multiple spokes, noticed inconsistency, requested homogenization
guidance: Verification responses: numbered list format, max 10 lines total, no verbose explanations unless errors found
